subject: Clarify: tier rollback mechanics & packaging credit mapping (pricing redline)
messages:
From: Pete Lawson <pete.lawson@cloudscale.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@cloudscale.com>, procure@cloudscale.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing schedule question — rollback and packaging credits

Tessa — thanks for the deck this morning. Two things came up in procurement review that we need clarified before legal will sign: 

1) Tier rollback: Section 3.2 describes an automatic rollback of discount tiers if monthly consumption drops below the band. Procurement is worried about a hard rollback that triggers immediately after a one-month dip (e.g., month 11 drops 20%). Can you confirm whether "rollback" is retroactive or forward-looking, and whether there's a grace buffer?

2) Packaging credits: Our billing and product teams want to understand how packaging credits apply when SKUs are consolidated mid-term. If we deprecate an SKU and move users to a bundled SKU, do credits carry forward or are they recalculated pro rata?

We attached our internal procurement checklist; please advise with specific redline language. If easier, we can jump on a 30m call with legal + billing.

Thanks,
Pete
VP Procurement, CloudScale

Attachments: cloudscale_procurement_checklist.pdf (stub)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Pete Lawson <pete.lawson@cloudscale.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing schedule question — rollback and packaging credits

Pete — appreciate the clear questions. Quick answers up front, longer notes below: 
- Rollback: we typically implement a forward-looking downgrade after a two-month buffer (we call it a "grace window") to avoid churn from short-term swings. Retroactive true-ups are limited to the prior 90 days unless otherwise negotiated.
- Packaging credits: credits follow active user instances for 60 days post-deprecation; after that billing re-maps pro rata to the new SKU unless the customer requests credit preservation in writing.

I'll loop in Karthik (pricing) and Laura (billing ops) for exact redline suggestions — attaching our latest pricing schedule for context. Happy to set a call; are you available Thu 23rd 10am PT?

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Pete Lawson <pete.lawson@cloudscale.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed redline language for tier rollback + packaging credits

Pete / Tessa — looping in suggested contract language below that legal can drop into the order form. I tried to be conservative to address procurement concerns while preserving operational guardrails. Please review: 

--- Proposed redline (pricing exhibit, Section 3.2) ---
"Monthly Adjusted Usage" means the total billable units attributable to Customer during a calendar month after application of prefix caching and applicable discounts. Where Monthly Adjusted Usage falls below the Minimum Usage Band for two (2) consecutive months, Redwood may apply a forward-looking adjustment to the Customer's pricing tier effective the first day of the following month. No retrospective price increases shall be applied more than ninety (90) days after the month in which usage occurred. Redwood agrees to apply a Grace Buffer equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the customer's prior rolling 3‑month average to prevent immediate downgrade due to transient dips.

--- Proposed redline (packaging credits, Section 4.1) ---
Credits associated with a deprecated SKU shall remain available to Customer for a transition period of sixty (60) days from deprecation notice. After the transition period, remaining credits will be applied pro rata against charges for the replacement SKU(s) unless Customer and Redwood agree in writing to preserve credit balances beyond the transition period. In the event of SKU consolidation initiated by Customer, Customer may elect to carry forward credit balances to the consolidated SKU upon written election at time of consolidation.

Operational notes: 
- The Grace Buffer calculation above uses rolling 3-month average to avoid oscillation around band thresholds.
- True-ups > 90 days require Sales and Finance approval (recorded in HubSpot).

If this tracks, Legal can format it as tracked changes. I also attach a short markup (tessa_redline_proposal.docx).

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Lawson <pete.lawson@cloudscale.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Billing implications & implementation constraints

Pete — quick operational clarifications from Billing Ops so procurement understands how this will behave on invoices: 

1) Grace Buffer: we'll compute the 3-month rolling average and subtract 15% to generate the buffer floor. During the 60-day transition for deprecated SKUs, we tag affected invoices with the original SKU code and a "transition" line so you can audit credit application.
2) System limits: our billing engine supports retroactive true-ups up to 90 days. Anything beyond requires a manual Finance journal entry and will be flagged as "manual adjustment" on the invoice (with supporting audit notes).
3) Packaging credit carry-forward: when Customer elects to carry forward credits at consolidation, Procurement will need to sign a simple Credit Preservation Addendum; we can pre-fill and share a template.

I've put proposed invoice examples into the Drive folder (link below). If legal wants different trigger language (e.g., 30% buffer instead of 15%), that will change the invoice band mapping and we should re-run the cost model.

Laura Bennett
Billing Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing schedule question — rollback and packaging credits

Team — this is very helpful, thanks. Procurement and legal reviewed Karthik's wording and asked for two small edits: 

1) Increase Grace Buffer to 20% for the first year of the agreement, after which the 15% default applies. This is to cover our expected seasonal ramp in year one.
2) Add a clause that any credit-preservation election must be made within the 60-day transition window and that preserved credits will be itemized on the next invoice.

We should adopt the Credit Preservation Addendum template and jump on the Thu 23rd 10am PT call (confirmed). For the redline, please circulate a tracked-change version ahead of the call so our legal can mark it up live.

Regards,
Pete
VP Procurement, CloudScale
